3_4_production_prevalence.conclusion: v3 = ~16% of real transactions alerted at production prevalence with precision ~0.75%; enriched-sample 43% precision / 25% alert rate is a 100x-prevalence artifact and must NOT be reported as production performance

7_temporal_drift.note: 2020 Jan-Feb present but <5 sampled fraud in the sample window bucket split; recall@1%FPR drops 0.458 -> 0.346 across 2018->2019, consistent with temporal degradation

8_pr_operating_points.note: investigator-relevant: even v2's 1.28% FPR yields only ~4% precision at production prevalence; extreme class imbalance dominates

5_cascade_interim.stage2_consensus: degenerates - members 0.94-0.97 correlated, cannot hold val recall>=0.99 at any bar above stage-1
5_cascade_interim.conclusion: stage-2 consensus adds nothing; single global threshold at the same val recall target has FEWER alerts than the v3 recall-max point - the curve, not the cascade, is binding

6_segmented_interim.note: segments degenerate on current model because err feature is CONSTANT 1.0 (see finding below) - segmentation re-test deferred to improved model

F1_err_feature_broken.detail: err (transaction-error flag) is 1.0 for 100% of val+test rows. Root cause: scripts/retrain_native_consistent.py:172 str(r['Errors?'] or '') - pandas NaN is truthy, so NaN or '' returns NaN -> str(NaN)='nan' -> non-empty -> err=1 for the ~98.4% of rows with NO error. Real error rows (~1.5%) also err=1. Feature is constant in training (dead weight) AND semantically mismatched with production (engine default errors='' -> err=0). Fix: NaN-safe parsing in BOTH the retrain raw build and native_features.py err line; parity re-test after fix.

state: v3 threshold deployment (altman_native_v3_20260904_133000) exists on disk from earlier work but its production-readiness claims are NOT yet re-verified (#9 pending); no website/audit/cert claims updated.

7b_channel_shift_finding.implication: validation window (2016-17) fraud is ~94% from 2016 and 86% of that is the ONLINE channel; the untouched test (2018-19) fraud is almost entirely chip/swipe IN-PERSON. The v2/v3 threshold was locked on an online-fraud wave that mostly vanishes at test time -> a channel-shift component of temporal drift, not pure calendar drift. Explains recall@1%FPR 0.458(2018)->0.346(2019) and why the 1%-FPR v2 operating point caught only ~44% of test fraud.
7b_channel_shift_finding.segment_experiment_note: segmented thresholds by risk tier (cold-start/online/pattern/mature) reallocate the same alert budget (test FPR 0.1605 vs global 0.1587) -> no alert reduction at >=99% recall; two-stage consensus cascade degenerates to stage-1 because member models are 0.94-0.97 correlated.

5_cascade_corrected.design: stage1: highest val threshold with val recall>=0.995 (locked on val). stage2: member-consensus bar b (all 3 members >= b among stage-1 alerts) tuned on val to hold recall>=0.99 while cutting alerts.
5_cascade_corrected.stage2_outcome: DEGENERATE -> no b keeps val recall>=0.99 at fewer alerts (members 0.94-0.97 correlated); cascade == stage-1 screen.
5_cascade_corrected.conclusion: two-stage consensus cascade does NOT reduce alerts at >=99% recall for this ensemble

6_segmented_corrected.design: segments designed a priori on feature semantics (cold-start / online / pattern-risk / mature-normal), per-segment thresholds locked on VALIDATION at segment recall>=0.99, err excluded (constant in deployed regime).
6_segmented_corrected.conclusion: segmented thresholds slightly raise recall (0.9991 vs 0.9954) at the SAME alert rate -> reallocation not reduction; no segmentation discovered that cuts alerts at >=99% recall
